Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dflq.qov.ph DILG OPINION NO. MEMORANDUM FOR SUBJECT DATE REGIONAL DIRECTOR MARIA LOURDES L. AGUSTIN, CESO Ill DILG-NationaI Capital Region LEGAL OPINION ON THE VALIDITY OF THE DEED OF DONATION ENTERED INTO BETWEEN THE QUEZON CITY GOVERNMENT AND THE DILG QUEZON CITY FIELD OFFICE [NCR-2024-06-10- 005] 21 We refer to your letter dated 03 June 2024, requesting the Department's opinion on the validity of the Deed of Donation executed and entered into between the Quezon City Government (hereinafter the "City"), represented by Mayor Ma. Josefina G. Belmonte and the Department, represented by Director Emmanuel D. Borromeo, CESO V of the DILG-Quezon City Field Office, in light of the provision under DILG Circular No. 2018- 101 delegating to the DILG Regional Director the authority to accept donations. Per your representation, the said donation involves the transfer of ownership of two (2) vehicles to the DILG-NCR for the specific use of DILG-Quezon City Field Office. We discuss. Under the Civil Code, a contract is a meeting of the minds, with respect to the other, to give something or to render some service. Article 1318 of the Civil Code provides: Art. 1318. There is no contract unless the following requisites concur: (I) Consent of the contracting parties; (2) Object certain which is the subject matter of the contract; and (3) Cause of the obligation which is established. Accordingly, for a contract to be valid, it must have the following essential elements: (I) consent of the contracting parties; (2) object certain, which is the subject matter of the contract; and (3) cause of the obligation which is established. Consent is manifested by the meeting of the offer and the acceptance of the thing and the cause, which are to constitute the contract. The contract is perfected at the moment there is a meeting of the minds upon the thing that is the object of the contract and the price. Delegation of Authority-Local Government Sector "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

In the present case, all the essential elements - consent, object and cause - are present. The Quezon City Government entered into an agreement with DILG-NCR. They agreed that the City Government would deliver two (2) vehicles to DILG-NCR for the specific use of the DILG-Quezon City Field Office. The two (2) vehicles constitute the object or subject matter of the contract. Considering the foregoing, since the contract of donation is entered into by the parties in accordance with the basic requirements of a standard contract, this Department's inclination is to recognize that contract as valid. Nonetheless, may we emphasize that under our laws, a contract that is executed by a person without authority or in excess of authority is an unenforceable contract. This type of contract cannot be given effect, unless properly ratified expressly or impliedly pursuant to Article 1403 in relation to Article 1317, both of the Civil Code of the Philippines, thus: "Article 1403. The following contracts are unenforceable, unless that are ratified: (1) Those entered into in the name of another person by one who has been given no authority or legal representation, or who has acted beyond his powers; xxx "Article 1317 No one may contract in the name of another without being authorized by the latter, or unless he has by law a right to represent him. A contract entered into in the name of another by one who has no authority or legal representation, or who has acted beyond his powers, shall be unenforceable, unless it is ratified, expressly or impliedly, by the person on whose behalf it has been executed, before it is revoked by the other contracting party." [Underscoring ours] It is to be noted that the lack of authority does not make the agreement void or inexistent. It merely bars suit for performance or breach. The defect in the contract can be cured by acknowledgment or ratification. The ratification of contract is explained in the case of Yasuma v. Heirs of Cecilio S. de Villa,et ap. "Ratification means that the principal voluntarily adopts, confirms and gives sanction to some unauthorized act of its agent on its behalf. It is this voluntary choice, knowingly mad, which amounts to a ratification of what was theretofore unauthorized and becomes the authorized act of the party so making the ratification. The substance of the doctrine is confirmation after conduct, amounting to a substitute for a prior authority. Ratification can be made either expressly or impliedly. Implied ratification may take various forms-like silence or acquiescence, act showing approval or adoption of the act, or acceptance and retention of benefits flowing therefrom. " 7 G.R. No. 150350, Aug 22, 2006 Page 2 of 3

In view of the foregoing, since Director Borromeo had no authority to sign the contract pursuant to DILG Circular No. 2018-10, ratification is always an option for DILG-NCR Regional Director in order to cure the defect in the contract. We hope to have guided you on the matter. This opinion is rendered based solely on the facts presented and our appreciation of the same without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of other government agencies and the courts.
